title: Just Noticeable Difference
text: Formally, Just Noticeable Difference (JND) can be defined as the magnitude of change in a stimulus necessary for it to be perceived as different from another stimulus, or as the smallest detectable difference between two stimuli (Stern and Johnson 2010).

title: SDT, ROC and Calibration
text:
Model
Suppose we want to perform binary classification on some data.

d1 <- rnorm(100, mean = 5, sd = 1)
d2 <- rnorm(100, mean = 4.5, sd = 1)
df <- tibble(d1, d2) %>% pivot_longer(cols = d1:d2)
df %>% head(5)

# A tibble: 5 × 2
  name  value
  <chr> <dbl>
1 d1     4.68
2 d2     5.08
3 d1     3.17
4 d2     4.76
5 d1     3.14


Let’s try a simple linear model:

simple_linear_regression <- lm(value ~ name, df)
summary(simple_linear_regression)


Call:
lm(formula = value ~ name, data = df)

Residuals:
    Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
-2.8692 -0.7429 -0.0209  0.6527  3.1788 

Coefficients:
            Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
(Intercept)   4.9791     0.1039   47.93   <2e-16 ***
named2       -0.3334     0.1469   -2.27   0.0243 *  
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

Residual standard error: 1.039 on 198 degrees of freedom
Multiple R-squared:  0.02536,   Adjusted R-squared:  0.02043 
F-statistic: 5.151 on 1 and 198 DF,  p-value: 0.02431


Let’s plot this!

df %>% ggplot(aes(y = value, x= name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  labs(y = "Default (1 = yes, 0 = no)",
       title = "Default outcome by balance") +
  theme_minimal()

`geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'
